title: Infrastructure funding gap and capital project approvals
subtitle: Bill 23 development charge losses, new crossing guard, BIA board, respectful workplace policy and council committee appointments
overview: Council received the 2022 asset management update, which shows the annual infrastructure funding gap has grown. Staff attributed the increase mainly to higher inflation and to more assets being added to the tracking system. A request to raise infrastructure reinvestment funding is expected with the 2023 budget on February 13.

Council approved early inclusion of several 2023 capital projects in the budget, including large-scale facility repairs, a fire pumper replacement, Waterloo Park master plan work, a culvert rehabilitation and sidewalks and trails linked to the LRT {{vote:m6}}. It also approved a new adult school crossing guard at Laurelwood Drive and American Beech Avenue, starting in January 2023 or sooner if someone is recruited {{vote:m7}}. Council confirmed the updated Respectful Workplace Policy {{vote:m5}}, the Uptown Waterloo BIA board for 2022 to 2026 {{vote:m2}}, and its own committee and board appointments {{vote:m8}}.

In questions, councillors raised Bill 23 and the loss of development charge revenue. Staff said the City has paused its new development charge study and will rely on its current by-law, and that an adaptation report and a reserve fund forecast were due the following week. Council also went into a closed session about a service agreement; the minutes report no outcome from it.

decisions.detail: Council approved including five 2023 projects in the capital budget ahead of the February 13, 2023 budget vote, with funding released January 1 for most and a funding release report to come for the Waterloo Park master plan work.
Council approved a warranted adult crossing guard at Laurelwood Drive and American Beech Avenue starting in January 2023, or sooner if a guard is recruited.
Council approved the updated Respectful Workplace Policy and Program and authorized the Mayor and Chief Administrative Officer to sign it.
Council approved the 15 appointments to the Uptown Waterloo Business Improvement Area board of directors for 2022 to 2026.
Council approved the 2022 appointments of its members to boards and committees and directed that the by-laws be enacted.

decisions.item: Asset management update and report cards
decisions.detail: Council received the 2022 asset management update and report cards for information.

debate: On asset management, staff said inflation was the main driver of the larger funding gap. One councillor asked whether the gap would be far smaller in a normal inflation year, and staff said it would not drop by anything close to that share.

Staff said the fleet looks relatively strong in the report cards partly because it has few assets and low data maturity, so results could change as data improves. Electric vehicles cost more and the fleet reserve is built around like-for-like replacement, so staff are looking at other funding such as green reserves and at charging infrastructure.
Staff said climate change costs are not yet built into the asset forecasts. They are waiting on the climate change plan for direction.

On the crossing guard, one councillor said the position's pay is very low for the commitment required and asked that it be reviewed in the budget. Staff agreed to take that into account in budget deliberations. Another councillor noted the intersection is heavily used by children.

On Bill 23, councillors worried about lost development charge revenue, the effect on parkland, recreation facilities and other amenities, and getting the City's message to the province before the legislature's break. Staff said the revenue loss would be significant and not all impacts are known yet. Staff also said the City's current development charge by-law delays some of the changes and that the reserve forecast would show how reserves are allocated.
